chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad ibn Isa al-Juhani from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah ibn A'yan and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Basir and Burayd al-Ajli and al-Fadl ibn Yasar from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) said:

"There is no zakat on the camels and cattle of the workers (or: on the camels and cattle themselves, depending on interpretation of 'al-'amalat' as workers or plural of 'amal/work'), rather the zakat is on the 'saimah' (the grazing livestock kept for profit), and whatever has not completed its year (hawl) at its owner, there is no zakat upon it; so when the year completes upon it, it becomes obligatory upon it."

key_terms.اَلسَّائِمَةِ: The grazing livestock kept for profit, which is the primary category for this zakat ruling.
key_terms.اَلْحَوْلُ: The lunar year of ownership required for zakat to become obligatory.
key_terms.اَلْعَوَامِلِ: The workers or those who manage the livestock; or plural of 'amal' referring to the livestock themselves in some readings.

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for zakat becoming obligatory on camels and cattle in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from the Ahl al-Bayt clarifies the specific conditions for zakat on livestock, distinguishing between 'saimah' (grazing animals kept for profit) and those not subject to this tax, while emphasizing the completion of the lunar year (hawl) as the trigger for obligation. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on precise criteria for wealth purification, ensuring that the tax is levied only on productive assets held for a full cycle, thereby protecting the general populace from undue burden.
